subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Enigma Machine
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Enigma Machine.

hook.text: Nazi Germany's Enigma machine could encrypt a message in 158 quintillion ways. The Allies broke it anyway.

buildup.text: Enigma used rotating wheels and plugboards to scramble messages. Each keystroke changed the encryption.

discovery.text: Polish mathematicians cracked early Enigma versions. Their work was passed to Britain before the war.

twist.text: Germany kept adding complexity. Each upgrade forced codebreakers to start from scratch again.

climax.text: Breaking Enigma was a relay race across nations and decades — not a single genius moment.

quiz.question: Who first cracked early versions of the Enigma machine?
